Symptom: PC cannot reach gateway or server
Evidence: show vlan brief, show interfaces fa0/1 switchport, ipconfig
Expected_Fault: PC switch port assigned to wrong VLAN
Expected_Fix: Assign Fa0/1 to VLAN 10
Verification: Ping gateway and server successfully
Notes: PC has VLAN 10 IP configuration but switch port is in VLAN 20

Symptom: PC cannot reach gateway/server
Evidence: VLAN and switchport outputs + IP/ping results
Expected_Fault: VLAN 10 missing on Switch1
Expected_Fix: Recreate VLAN 10 and assign required ports
Verification: Gateway and server ping successfully
Notes: VLAN itself was deleted

Topology: PC1->Switch1->Switch2->PC2; Switch1 Fa0/2 <-> Switch2 Fa0/1 is trunk
Symptom: PC1 cannot reach PC2
Evidence: show interfaces trunk on Switch1/Switch2; show vlan brief on Switch1/Switch2; ipconfig on PC1/PC2; failed ping PC1 -> PC2
Expected_Fault: VLAN 10 not allowed on trunk
Expected_Fix: Allow VLAN 10 on trunk
Verification: PC1 successfully pings PC2
Notes: VLAN 10 exists on both switches and access ports are correctly assigned, but VLAN 10 is not allowed on the Switch1-Switch2 trunk

Symptom: PC1 does not receive a vali 192.168.10.x address
Evidence: ipconfig, show ip dhcp pool, show ip dhcp binding, show running-config | section dhcp, failed ping to 192.168.10.1
Expected_Fault: DHCP pool configured with wrong network
Expected_Fix: Configure DHCP pool for 192.168.10.0/24
Verification: PC1 receives 192.168.10.x address and can ping 192.168.10.1
Notes: DHCP service is present, but the pool network does not match the LAN

Symptom: PC1 cannot reach default gateway
Evidence: show ip interface brief, show interfaces g0/0, ipconfig, failed ping
Expected_Fault: R1 G0/0 administratively shut down
Expected_Fix: no shutdown on Router1 G0/0
Verification: G0/0 becomes up/up and PC1 csuccessfully pings 192.168.10.1
Notes: Physical connection is intact, but the router interface is administratively disabled

Symptom: Connectivity fails after two hosts are configured with the same IP
Evidence: ipconfig, arp -a on PC1/PC2, failed gateway pings
Expected_Fault: PC1 and PC2 configured with the same IP address 192.168.10.10
Expected_Fix: Assign PC2 a unique IP address, 192.168.10.20
Verification: PC1 and PC2 successfully communicate and can reach 192.168.10.1
Notes: Duplicate IP addresses cause an IP address conflict and connectivity problems

Symptom: PC1 cannot reach PC2 on remote LAN
Evidence: show ip route, show running-config, ipconfig, failed ping
Expected_Fault: R1 has incorrect static route next hop 10.0.0.3
Expected_Fix: Change next hop to 10.0.0.2
Verification: PC1 successfully pings 192.168.20.10
Notes: Remote network exists, but R1 forwards traffic toward an incorrect next-hop address

Symptom: IP connectivity works but hostname resolution fails
Evidence: ipconfig, successful DNS-server ping, failed nslookup
Expected_Fault: PC1 configured with incorrect DNS server 192.168.10.200
Expected_Fix: Set DNS server to 192.168.10.100
Verification: nslookup cisco.local successfully resolves
Notes: Network connectivity remains available; only name resolution is affected

Symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with PC2; ping shows 100% loss
Evidence: show interfaces status on Switch1 shows Fa0/2 as notconnect; PC1 and PC2 have valid IP addresses in the same subnet
Expected_Fault: Ethernet cable between Switch1 Fa0/2 and PC2 Fa0 is disconnected
Expected_Fix: Reconnect the Ethernet cable between Switch1 Fa0/2 and PC2 Fa0
Verification: Ping PC2 from PC1:ping 192.168.10.20: expected0% packet loss
Notes: Physical link should show connected/green after reconnecting the cable
Rule Suggested Fix: Check IP addressing and network connectivity

Symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with the switch;Ethernet link is not operational
Evidence: show interfaces status shows that Fa0/1 is not in the normal connected state; PC1 has valid IP configuration
Expected_Fault: Wrong Ethernet cable type used between PC1 Fa0 and Switch1 Fa0/1
Expected_Fix: Replace the incorrect cable with the appropriate Ethernet cable
Verification: show interfaces status shows Fa0/1 as connected and the physical link becomes active
Notes: Wrong cable type used; physical link is down

Symptom: PC1 cannot reach PC2; ping shows packet loss
Evidence: show ip interface brief shows R1 interfaces up/up; show arp shows an incorrect MAC address mapped to 192.168.20.10; ping fails
Expected_Fault: Incorrect static ARP entry for PC2
Expected_Fix: Remove the incorrect ARP entry using no arp 192.168.20.10
Verification: ping 192.168.20.10 succeeds with 0% packet loss and ARP table shows the correct MAC
Notes: Incorrect MAC mapped to PC2 IP

Symptom: PC1 can ping the server but cannot access its HTTP webpage
Evidence: Ping to 192.168.10.20 succeeds; HTTP webpage fails to load; Server HTTP service is Off
Expected_Fault: HTTP service disabled on the server
Expected_Fix: Enable HTTP service on the Server
Verification: HTTP webpage loads successfully and ping shows 0% packet loss
Notes: IP connectivity works but HTTP service is unavailable

Symptom: R1 cannot discover R2 using CDP although IP connectivity works
Evidence: show cdp neighbors does not display R2; show cdp interface g0/1 shows CDP disabled; G0/1 is up/up and ping to R2 succeeds
Expected_Fault: CDP disabled on R1 G0/1
Expected_Fix: Enable CDP on R1 G0/1 using cdp enable
Verification: R2 appears in show cdp neighbors and show cdp neighbors detail
Notes: CDP disabled on R1 G0/1 while IP connectivity remains functional

Symptom: SW3 unexpectedly becomes the STP Root Bridge
Evidence: show spanning-tree and show spanning-tree vlan 1 show SW3 as Root; STP priority on SW3 is lower than SW1
Expected_Fault: Incorrect STP priority configured on SW3
Expected_Fix: Set SW3 VLAN 1 priority to 32768
Verification: show spanning-tree vlan 1 confirms SW1 is Root Bridge and SW3 is non-root
Notes: SW3 priority was set to 0, causing it to win the Root Bridge election

Symptom: EtherChannel is not correctly bundling both links
Evidence: show etherchannel summary shows inconsistent channel membership; SW2 Fa0/2 is assigned to channel-group 2 while the other member ports use channel-group 1
Expected_Fault: Switch2 assigned to the wrong EtherChannel group
Expected_Fix: Remove Fa0/2 from channel-group 2 and assign it to channel-group 1 using PAgP
Verification: show etherchannel summary shows Po1(SU) with Fa0/1(P) and Fa0/2(P) on both switches
Notes: One physical member was assigned to a different channel group, preventing consistent EtherChannel bundling

Symptom: R1/R2 cannot discover the neighboring router through CDP, while IP connectivity still works
Evidence: show cdp neighbors, show cdp interface g0/0, successful ping 192.168.20.2
Expected_Fault: CDP disabled on R1 G0/0 using no cdp enable
Expected_Next_Command: show cdp neighbors; show cdp interface g0/0
Expected_Fix: Enable CDP on R1 G0/0 using cdp enable
Verification: show cdp neighbors shows the neighboring router and ping succeeds
Notes: IP connectivity is working, but CDP neighbor information is missing while CDP is disabled; after the fix, the neighbor information returns.

Topology: PC1 → Switch1 → Router1 → Router2 → DHCP Server
Symptom: PC1 displays 'DHCP request failed' and remains without a valid IP address because the DHCP server is on a remote network.
Evidence: PC DHCP request failed, show ip route, running configuration.
Expected_Fault: Missing ip helper-address
Expected_Fix: ip helper-address on the client-facing router interface.
Verification: PC receives a valid DHCP address and can ping gateway/server
Notes: Verify end-to-end connectivity first. Capture DHCP failure and router configuration before fixing. Record the missing helper-address condition and confirm routing in both directions.

Symptom: The trunk is operational, but untagged/native VLAN traffic behaves unexpectedly between switches.
Evidence: show interfaces trunk, show vlan brief
Expected_Fault: Different native VLAN configured on trunk ends.
Expected_Fix: Configure the same native VLAN on both switches
Verification: Verify trunk and successful VLAN connectivity
Notes: Compare trunk settings on both ends. Record each native VLAN before correction and verify both ends match afterward.

Symptom: Hosts in the same VLAN on different switches cannot communicate although access ports appear correct.
Evidence: show interfaces trunk, show interfaces switchport
Expected_Fault: Incorrect DTP negotiation
Expected_Fix: Configure compatible DTP modes or force trunk.
Verification: Trunk becomes active
Notes: Check the trunk allowed-VLAN list before changing access ports. Capture the required VLAN missing from the trunk and verify forwarding after correction.

Symptom: A host cannot communicate with devices in its intended VLAN because its access port belongs to another VLAN.
Evidence: show vtp status; show vlan brief
Expected_Fault: Incorrect VTP domain
Expected_Fix: Set the correct VTP domain on participating switches
Verification: Verify VLAN database propagation
Notes: Confirm intended VLAN and IP network. Record the incorrect port mapping, correct only the affected interface, and verify connectivity.

Symptom: VLAN information created on one switch does not synchronize to the neighboring VTP switch.
Evidence: show vtp status; show vlan brief
Expected_Fault: VTP server/client mode mismatch
Expected_Fix: Correct VTP operating modes and synchronize VLAN database
Verification: Verify VLAN appears
Notes: Compare VTP domain, mode, and revision information. Verify the VLAN database after synchronization.

Symptom: Connectivity works, but STP selects an inefficient path because an unintended switch becomes root bridge.
Evidence: show spanning-tree
Expected_Fault: Incorrect STP root bridge
Expected_Fix: Set intended root priority
Verification: Verify root bridge and forwarding path
Notes: Document the current root bridge and port roles. Change priority carefully and confirm the intended switch becomes root.

Symptom: An access interface becomes err-disabled after receiving BPDUs, causing loss of connectivity.
Evidence: show spanning-tree; show running-config
Expected_Fault: PortFast configured on wrong port
Expected_Fix: Apply PortFast only to intended edge/access port
Verification: Verify STP state
Notes: Capture interface and STP evidence before recovery. Identify the BPDU source, correct the cause, then safely restore the port.

Symptom: A switch port restricts or shuts down traffic after more MAC addresses are learned than allowed.
Evidence: show interfaces status; show errdisable recovery; show spanning-tree
Expected_Fault: BPDU Guard triggered
Expected_Fix: Remove unintended BPDU source or correct BPDU Guard placement, then recover port
Verification: Verify interface is connected/forwarding
Notes: Record port-security status, violation count, and secure MAC addresses. Confirm authorization before changing limits.

Symptom: A replacement device cannot connect because the port still expects an old sticky MAC address.
Evidence: show spanning-tree detail; show spanning-tree
Expected_Fault: Root Guard is blocking the port
Expected_Fix: Correct/remove Root Guard where inappropriate
Verification: Verify port returns to expected STP state
Notes: Collect the existing sticky MAC entry. Remove/update only the obsolete entry and verify the new authorized device.

Symptom: EtherChannel forms partially or fails because member interface settings are inconsistent.
Evidence: show port-security; show interfaces status
Expected_Fault: Port-security maximum MAC limit exceeded
Expected_Fix: Set appropriate maximum or remove unauthorized device
Verification: Verify secure port and connectivity
Notes: Compare channel members: switchport mode, VLAN/trunk settings, speed, duplex, and channel settings. Verify all members bundle.

Symptom: EtherChannel negotiation fails because both ends use incompatible protocols or modes.
Evidence: show port-security address; show port-security
Expected_Fault: Sticky MAC violation
Expected_Fix: Clear/update sticky MAC configuration appropriately
Verification: Verify correct secure MAC is learned
Notes: Check channel summary on both sides. Configure one compatible protocol and verify port-channel and members are bundled.

Symptom: A device MAC address is learned on an unexpected switch port, suggesting incorrect physical connectivity.
Evidence: show port-security
Expected_Fault: Wrong violation mode
Expected_Fix: Configure intended violation mode
Verification: Reconnect/test endpoint and verify behavior
Notes: Generate traffic and capture the MAC table. Trace cabling, correct the physical path, and confirm the MAC learns on the intended port.

Symptom: Local connectivity works, but unknown remote networks fail because no gateway of last resort exists.
Evidence: show mac address-table; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Incorrect static MAC entry
Expected_Fix: Correct/remove the incorrect static MAC entry
Verification: Verify MAC is learned on correct port
Notes: Record the routing table before fixing. Add only the required default route and verify remote reachability.

Symptom: A static route exists but traffic fails because its next-hop address is incorrect or unreachable.
Evidence: show mac address-table dynamic; show interfaces status
Expected_Fault: Incorrect physical connection or MAC learning path
Expected_Fix: Correct cabling/port assignment
Verification: Verify MAC appears on expected interface
Notes: Validate next-hop reachability. Capture the incorrect route, replace it, and verify routing table plus end-to-end ping.

Symptom: Traffic uses the backup path while the primary path is healthy because administrative distances are incorrectly prioritized.
Evidence: show ip route; show ip interface brief
Expected_Fault: Missing default route
Expected_Fix: Configure correct default route
Verification: Ping remote network and verify route
Notes: Document both routes and AD values. Correct the floating route so it activates only when the primary path fails.

Topology: R1 with primary and backup paths
Symptom: A remote network is missing because one connected network is not advertised by RIP.
Evidence: show ip route; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Incorrect administrative distance on floating static route
Expected_Fix: Correct static-route administrative distance
Verification: Verify preferred route is installed
Notes: Check RIP participating networks. Add the missing advertisement and verify neighboring routers learn the route.

Symptom: RIP routers do not exchange routes correctly because incompatible RIP versions are configured.
Evidence: show ip route; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Incorrect static-route next hop
Expected_Fix: Correct next-hop address
Verification: Ping destination and verify route
Notes: Capture protocol settings on both routers. Standardize the version and verify route exchange.

Symptom: EIGRP neighbors do not form despite working physical and IP connectivity.
Evidence: show ip protocols; show ip route
Expected_Fault: Missing RIP network advertisement
Expected_Fix: Advertise the missing connected network in RIP
Verification: Verify RIP route appears
Notes: Verify basic connectivity, compare EIGRP AS numbers, capture missing neighbors, then verify adjacency and routes.

Symptom: EIGRP adjacency does not form on a transit link because hello packets are suppressed.
Evidence: show ip protocols; show ip route
Expected_Fault: RIP auto-summary causing incorrect routing
Expected_Fix: Disable auto-summary where appropriate
Verification: Verify specific routes are learned
Notes: Identify the passive interface. Remove passive status only from the router-to-router link and verify adjacency.

Symptom: A required interface does not participate in EIGRP because its network statement or wildcard is wrong.
Evidence: show ip eigrp neighbors; show ip protocols
Expected_Fault: Mismatched EIGRP autonomous-system number
Expected_Fix: Use the same EIGRP AS number on both routers
Verification: Verify neighbor adjacency
Notes: Compare interface IP addresses with EIGRP statements. Correct the wildcard precisely and avoid enabling unintended interfaces.

Symptom: OSPF routers fail to form adjacency because the shared interfaces use different area IDs.
Evidence: show ip protocols; show ip eigrp topology
Expected_Fault: Incorrect EIGRP wildcard/network statement
Expected_Fix: Correct the EIGRP network statement
Verification: Verify route/neighbor information
Notes: Collect neighbor/interface information from both routers. Align the area and verify adjacency reaches FULL.

Symptom: An expected OSPF neighbor is missing because the transit interface is configured as passive.
Evidence: show ip protocols; show ip eigrp neighbors
Expected_Fault: Passive-interface prevents EIGRP hellos
Expected_Fix: Remove passive-interface from the EIGRP transit interface
Verification: Verify neighbor becomes FULL/established
Notes: Confirm which interface should form adjacency. Remove passive status only from the transit link.

Symptom: An intended interface is not participating in OSPF because of an incorrect wildcard mask.
Evidence: show ip ospf interface; show ip protocols
Expected_Fault: Wrong OSPF wildcard mask
Expected_Fix: Correct the OSPF network statement/wildcard
Verification: Verify adjacency and route
Notes: Match the interface address against the OSPF statement. Correct the wildcard and verify OSPF activation.

Symptom: OSPF routers have IP connectivity but cannot establish adjacency because authentication settings differ.
Evidence: show ip ospf interface; show ip protocols
Expected_Fault: Passive-interface blocks OSPF hellos
Expected_Fix: Remove passive-interface from transit interface
Verification: Verify adjacency
Notes: Compare authentication type and key settings on both ends. Apply matching settings and verify stable adjacency.

Symptom: Traffic reaches the destination but follows a less efficient OSPF path due to an incorrect interface cost.
Evidence: show ip ospf interface; show ip ospf neighbor
Expected_Fault: Incorrect OSPF network type
Expected_Fix: Configure matching/intended OSPF network type
Verification: Verify expected adjacency behavior
Notes: Capture current route and metrics. Adjust only the relevant cost and verify the preferred path changes.

Symptom: Gateway redundancy fails because routers do not agree on HSRP group or virtual gateway settings.
Evidence: show ip ospf interface; show ip route
Expected_Fault: Incorrect OSPF interface cost
Expected_Fix: Correct interface OSPF cost
Verification: Verify routing table selects intended path
Notes: Document active/standby state and virtual IP. Standardize settings and test normal operation plus failover.

Symptom: A network is unreachable because the required router interface is administratively down.
Evidence: show ip ospf; show ip ospf neighbor
Expected_Fault: Duplicate/conflicting OSPF router ID
Expected_Fix: Assign unique router IDs and restart/reload OSPF process as needed
Verification: Verify unique router IDs and adjacency
Notes: Distinguish administrative shutdown from physical failure. Record initial status, enable the interface, and verify recovery.

Symptom: A BGP session remains inactive because remote AS does not match the peer's actual AS.
Evidence: show ip bgp summary; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Incorrect BGP remote AS
Expected_Fix: Correct neighbor remote-AS configuration
Verification: Verify BGP state becomes Established
Notes: Verify IP reachability, compare AS configuration, correct the neighbor statement, and confirm Established state.

Symptom: BGP adjacency is established but a required prefix is absent from advertisements.
Evidence: show ip bgp summary; show running-config
Expected_Fault: BGP neighbor shutdown
Expected_Fix: Remove neighbor shutdown
Verification: Verify Established state
Notes: Check BGP and main routing tables. Ensure the exact prefix exists locally and verify peer advertisement.

Symptom: A BGP route is visible but unusable because its advertised next hop is unreachable.
Evidence: show ip bgp; show ip protocols
Expected_Fault: Missing BGP network advertisement
Expected_Fix: Advertise the intended network in BGP
Verification: Verify route appears in BGP table
Notes: Separate control-plane from data-plane troubleshooting. Verify next-hop reachability and confirm the route becomes usable.

Symptom: An IPv6 host does not obtain usable global addressing or a default route through SLAAC.
Evidence: show ip bgp; show ip route
Expected_Fault: Incorrect BGP next-hop reachability/behavior
Expected_Fix: Correct next-hop handling and underlying reachability
Verification: Verify route is usable
Notes: Check router IPv6 configuration and advertisements. Record host state, correct router settings, and verify address/gateway acquisition.

Symptom: A remote IPv6 network is unreachable because a static route points to the wrong next hop or interface.
Evidence: show ipv6 interface; show running-config
Expected_Fault: IPv6 Router Advertisement/SLAAC disabled
Expected_Fix: Enable IPv6 forwarding/RA on the LAN interface as required
Verification: Verify IPv6 address appears on host
Notes: Validate the IPv6 next-hop path. Correct the route precisely and verify table plus end-to-end connectivity.

Symptom: A legitimate source is blocked even though basic routing is correct.
Evidence: show ipv6 route; show ipv6 interface
Expected_Fault: Incorrect IPv6 static-route next hop
Expected_Fix: Correct IPv6 next-hop/static route
Verification: Verify IPv6 ping
Notes: Inspect ACL entries, sequence logic, and placement. Preserve intended security policy while correcting the blocking rule.

Symptom: Connectivity exists, but an application fails because an extended ACL uses the wrong protocol or port.
Evidence: show ipv6 ospf neighbor; show ipv6 ospf interface
Expected_Fault: OSPFv3 process/interface configuration missing
Expected_Fix: Enable/correct OSPFv3 on the transit interface
Verification: Verify OSPFv3 neighbor and route
Notes: Confirm required protocol/port. Capture the rule, correct the service match, and verify intended traffic.

Symptom: ACL rules appear correct but traffic is blocked because the ACL is applied in the wrong direction.
Evidence: show access-lists; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Standard ACL blocks legitimate source
Expected_Fix: Correct ACL source/permit rule
Verification: Verify permitted ping/application access
Notes: Identify interface and direction exactly. Move the ACL carefully and retest both permitted and denied traffic.

Symptom: Internal hosts cannot create translations because NAT inside/outside roles are assigned to wrong interfaces.
Evidence: show access-lists; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Extended ACL has wrong protocol/port rule
Expected_Fix: Correct protocol/port permit/deny rule
Verification: Verify required service and blocked service behavior
Notes: Document NAT roles and statistics. Correct role assignment and verify translations with generated traffic.

Symptom: Internal hosts fail to access outside networks because the NAT ACL does not match the inside subnet.
Evidence: show ip interface; show access-lists
Expected_Fault: ACL applied in wrong direction
Expected_Fix: Apply ACL inbound/outbound on intended interface/direction
Verification: Verify traffic behavior
Notes: Compare addressing plan with NAT ACL. Correct network/wildcard and verify eligible hosts translate.

Symptom: Multiple hosts cannot reliably share a public address because NAT is configured without overload.
Evidence: show ip nat translations; show ip nat statistics; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Incorrect inside/outside interface designation
Expected_Fix: Correct `ip nat inside` and `ip nat outside` placement
Verification: Verify translation and connectivity
Notes: Confirm translation behavior. Add PAT overload and verify simultaneous translations for multiple hosts.

Symptom: A client receives an IP address but cannot reach remote networks because DHCP supplies the wrong default gateway.
Evidence: show ip nat translations; show ip nat statistics
Expected_Fault: NAT pool exhausted
Expected_Fix: Increase/adjust address pool or use PAT as appropriate
Verification: Verify additional clients translate
Notes: Record full client configuration. Correct DHCP gateway option, renew lease, and verify gateway plus remote connectivity.

Symptom: New clients fail to obtain addresses while earlier clients work because the DHCP pool is exhausted.
Evidence: show ip nat translations; show ip nat statistics
Expected_Fault: Missing PAT overload
Expected_Fix: Configure PAT with overload
Verification: Verify multiple translations
Notes: Inspect pool utilization and leases. Record exhaustion, expand capacity or reclaim addresses, and verify a new lease.

Symptom: A server is reachable by IP but not hostname because the client uses an incorrect DNS server.
Evidence: show clock; show ntp status; show ntp associations
Expected_Fault: Incorrect NTP server configuration
Expected_Fix: Correct NTP server address/configuration
Verification: Verify NTP synchronization
Notes: Use IP connectivity to isolate DNS. Capture DNS settings, correct server address, and verify hostname resolution.

Symptom: Device time remains unsynchronized because the configured NTP server is incorrect or unreachable.
Evidence: show running-config; show snmp
Expected_Fault: Incorrect SNMP community string
Expected_Fix: Correct SNMP community/access configuration
Verification: Verify SNMP polling
Notes: Check reachability before NTP status. Record association state, correct server configuration, and verify synchronization.

Symptom: Device events occur but no logs reach the centralized Syslog server because logging destination is incorrect.
Evidence: show logging; show running-config
Expected_Fault: Wrong syslog destination address
Expected_Fix: Correct logging host/destination configuration
Verification: Generate event and verify server receives log
Notes: Confirm Syslog reachability and configuration. Correct destination and trigger a test event to verify reception.

Symptom: A client detects the SSID but cannot authenticate because its security settings differ from the access point.
Evidence: show running-config on AP/router; client wireless settings
Expected_Fault: Incorrect WPA2/WPA3 security key/mode
Expected_Fix: Match SSID/security mode/key on client and AP
Verification: Reconnect client and verify IP/connectivity
Notes: Compare SSID, authentication, encryption, and credentials systematically. Correct mismatch and verify association, IP, gateway, and connectivity.

Symptom: PC1 is physically connected to Switch1 but cannot communicate with any device on the network. The interface appears inactive despite the cable being connected.
Evidence: Switch1 interface status shows down/down or err-disabled condition. Interface counters may show no received frames.
Expected_Fault: Faulty Ethernet cable or incorrect physical interface connection prevents Layer 1 communication.
Expected_Fix: Replace the faulty cable and reconnect PC1 to the correct Switch1 Ethernet port.
Verification: Confirm the interface changes to up/up and verify successful ping from PC1 to another host.
Notes: Check physical connectivity first before investigating IP addressing or routing problems.

Symptom: PC1 has a correct IPv4 address and default gateway but cannot reach Router1 or other remote networks.
Evidence: arp -a on PC1 shows an incomplete or incorrect MAC entry for the default gateway address.
Expected_Fault: ARP resolution failure prevents PC1 from learning the MAC address of its gateway.
Expected_Fix: Clear the incorrect ARP entry and verify Layer 2 connectivity between PC1 and Router1.
Verification: Ping the gateway again and confirm a valid gateway MAC address appears in the ARP table.
Notes: ARP converts a known IPv4 address into the required destination MAC address for local delivery.

Symptom: PC1 and PC2 are intended to communicate in VLAN 10 but ping fails even though both devices are connected to the same switch.
Evidence: show vlan brief shows one of the access ports assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10.
Expected_Fault: Incorrect switchport VLAN assignment places the hosts in different broadcast domains.
Expected_Fix: Configure both required access interfaces using switchport access vlan 10.
Verification: Verify both ports belong to VLAN 10 and confirm successful ping between PC1 and PC2.
Notes: Devices must belong to the same VLAN and IP subnet for direct Layer 2 communication.

Topology: Switch1 — Switch2 with VLAN10 and VLAN20
Symptom: Devices in VLAN 10 work locally on each switch but cannot communicate across Switch1 and Switch2.
Evidence: show interfaces trunk shows the inter-switch interface is operating as an access port instead of a trunk.
Expected_Fault: The link between switches is not configured for IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tagging.
Expected_Fix: Configure the inter-switch link as a trunk and allow the required VLANs.
Verification: Confirm trunk status is active and test communication between same-VLAN hosts on different switches.
Notes: Trunk links carry traffic for multiple VLANs by attaching VLAN identification tags to frames.

Symptom: Network connectivity becomes unstable after adding redundant links between switches, with ports frequently changing forwarding states.
Evidence: show spanning-tree displays unexpected port roles or incorrect RSTP configuration on one switch.
Expected_Fault: RSTP is disabled or inconsistent, causing improper handling of redundant Layer 2 paths.
Expected_Fix: Enable Rapid PVST or configure consistent RSTP mode across all participating switches.
Verification: Confirm stable root bridge selection and verify redundant ports have correct forwarding or alternate roles.
Notes: RSTP provides faster convergence than traditional STP after topology changes.

Symptom: PC1 cannot communicate with its configured default gateway although the Ethernet connection is operational.
Evidence: PC1 address is 192.168.10.10/24 while the gateway interface is configured in network 192.168.20.0/24.
Expected_Fault: Incorrect IPv4 subnet configuration places the host and gateway in different IP networks.
Expected_Fix: Correct the PC1 IPv4 address and subnet mask so they match the gateway network.
Verification: Ping the default gateway and verify that packets are successfully delivered.
Notes: Always verify IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway before troubleshooting higher-layer protocols.

Symptom: PC1 can access some network services but ICMP ping requests to PC2 consistently fail.
Evidence: ACL or interface configuration shows ICMP echo packets being denied while other IP traffic is permitted.
Expected_Fault: ICMP traffic is specifically blocked by a filtering rule or access control configuration.
Expected_Fix: Modify the ACL to permit required ICMP traffic or remove the incorrect deny statement.
Verification: Run ping and traceroute tests to confirm ICMP connectivity is restored.
Notes: ICMP is commonly used for connectivity testing, error reporting, ping, and traceroute operations.

Symptom: A TCP-based application cannot establish a session with Server1 even though basic IP connectivity is successful.
Evidence: Ping succeeds, but TCP connection attempts fail because the destination port is closed or blocked.
Expected_Fault: TCP three-way handshake cannot complete due to unavailable or filtered destination service port.
Expected_Fix: Enable the required service or allow the TCP port through the firewall or ACL.
Verification: Confirm the TCP connection establishes successfully and the application becomes reachable.
Notes: TCP requires SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK messages to establish a reliable connection.

Symptom: A UDP-based service produces intermittent communication failures without clear connection error messages.
Evidence: IP connectivity is successful, but UDP packets are not reaching the expected application port.
Expected_Fault: Incorrect UDP port configuration or filtering prevents datagrams from reaching the service.
Expected_Fix: Correct the UDP destination port configuration and permit the required UDP traffic.
Verification: Test the UDP application again and verify packets are received by Server1.
Notes: UDP is connectionless and does not provide handshake, acknowledgment, or guaranteed delivery.

Symptom: PC1 can ping WebServer successfully but cannot open the website using HTTP.
Evidence: Browser connection fails and Server1 HTTP service is disabled or port 80 is unavailable.
Expected_Fault: HTTP application service is not running on the web server.
Expected_Fix: Enable the HTTP service and ensure TCP port 80 is available.
Verification: Open the browser and access the server using its IPv4 address or configured hostname.
Notes: Successful ping only proves IP connectivity; application-layer services must also be operational.

Symptom: The secure website cannot be accessed using HTTPS although the same server responds correctly through HTTP.
Evidence: HTTP service works, but HTTPS port 443 or secure service configuration is disabled.
Expected_Fault: HTTPS service is unavailable or TCP port 443 is blocked.
Expected_Next_Command: Check HTTPS service and port configuration
Expected_Fix: Enable HTTPS service and allow TCP port 443 through relevant filtering devices.
Verification: Access the website using HTTPS and confirm the secure connection is established.
Notes: HTTPS provides encrypted communication by combining HTTP with TLS/SSL security mechanisms.

Symptom: PC1 can ping FTPServer but file upload and download operations cannot be performed.
Evidence: FTP client cannot authenticate or the FTP service is disabled on Server1.
Expected_Fault: FTP server service or user authentication configuration is incorrect.
Expected_Fix: Enable FTP service and configure valid username and password credentials.
Verification: Log in using FTP credentials and successfully transfer a test file.
Notes: FTP uses separate control and data communication and requires proper server authentication.

Symptom: Router1 fails while attempting to back up or restore its configuration from a TFTP server.
Evidence: Ping to TFTPServer succeeds, but the copy command returns a transfer timeout or file access error.
Expected_Fault: TFTP service is disabled or the specified file name/server location is incorrect.
Expected_Fix: Enable the TFTP service and verify server IP address and requested file name.
Verification: Run the configuration copy operation again and confirm successful file transfer.
Notes: TFTP uses UDP and does not provide authentication, making it simpler but less secure than FTP.

Symptom: Users can connect to the network but outgoing email messages remain unsent.
Evidence: Mail client shows SMTP connection failure and the SMTP service on MailServer is unavailable.
Expected_Fault: SMTP service is disabled or incorrectly configured for outgoing email delivery.
Expected_Fix: Enable SMTP and configure the correct outgoing mail server settings.
Verification: Send a test email and confirm successful delivery to another configured user.
Notes: SMTP is primarily responsible for sending and forwarding email messages between clients and servers.

Symptom: A user can send emails successfully but cannot download received messages to the mail client.
Evidence: SMTP configuration works, while POP3 service or mailbox retrieval settings are disabled.
Expected_Fault: POP3 service is unavailable or the incoming mail client configuration is incorrect.
Expected_Fix: Enable POP3 service and configure correct incoming server credentials.
Verification: Retrieve received messages successfully using the configured mail client.
Notes: POP3 generally downloads emails from the server to the local email client.

Symptom: Email users cannot synchronize folders and messages between multiple devices.
Evidence: Mail server is reachable but IMAP service is disabled or incorrectly configured.
Expected_Fault: IMAP protocol service is unavailable, preventing server-side mailbox synchronization.
Expected_Fix: Enable IMAP service and configure the correct incoming mail settings.
Verification: Log in from multiple clients and verify that mailbox folders synchronize correctly.
Notes: IMAP keeps emails primarily on the server and supports synchronized access from multiple devices.

Symptom: PC1 cannot remotely access Router1 using Telnet even though the router responds to ping requests.
Evidence: VTY lines do not permit Telnet or no password/login configuration is present.
Expected_Fault: Telnet remote access is not properly configured on Router1 VTY lines.
Expected_Fix: Configure VTY lines with login authentication and permit Telnet access if required.
Verification: Establish a Telnet session from PC1 and verify successful router CLI access.
Notes: Telnet transmits credentials and data without encryption and should only be used in controlled lab environments.

Symptom: Secure remote login to Router1 fails while normal network connectivity remains functional.
Evidence: Router1 has an IP address, but SSH version, domain name, RSA keys, or VTY transport settings are missing.
Expected_Fault: SSH server prerequisites are incomplete, preventing secure session establishment.
Expected_Fix: Configure hostname, domain name, local user, RSA keys, SSH version 2, and VTY SSH transport.
Verification: Connect from PC1 using SSH and authenticate successfully with configured credentials.
Notes: SSH provides encrypted remote CLI access and is preferred over Telnet for secure administration.

Symptom: The network monitoring system cannot collect interface and device statistics from Router1 and Switch1.
Evidence: SNMP polling requests fail because the community string or SNMP configuration does not match.
Expected_Fault: Incorrect SNMP community string or missing SNMP agent configuration prevents monitoring communication.
Expected_Fix: Configure the correct SNMP community and access permissions on the monitored devices.
Verification: Perform SNMP polling again and verify device information is received by the monitoring system.
Notes: SNMP allows centralized monitoring and management of network devices and operational statistics.

Symptom: PC1 has connectivity but experiences very slow communication, packet loss, and inconsistent application performance.
Evidence: Interface statistics show excessive collisions, late collisions, or duplex mismatch errors on the connected port.
Expected_Fault: Ethernet speed or duplex settings are mismatched between PC1 and Switch1.
Expected_Fix: Configure both sides for compatible speed and duplex settings or enable auto-negotiation consistently.
Verification: Monitor interface counters and confirm errors stop increasing during communication tests.
Notes: Duplex mismatch can allow partial connectivity while causing severe performance degradation and packet errors.

Symptom: PC1 has network connectivity, but the connection speed is lower than expected during normal data transfer.
Evidence: Interface status shows the link is operational, but negotiated speed is lower than the expected interface capability.
Expected_Fault: Ethernet interface speed negotiation selected an unintended lower speed.
Expected_Fix: Configure compatible speed settings or enable auto-negotiation on both connected interfaces.
Verification: Confirm the interface negotiates the expected speed and basic connectivity remains stable.
Notes: This issue mainly affects performance and does not completely stop communication.

Symptom: PC1 initially experiences a short delay when communicating with a newly contacted device on the local network.
Evidence: The ARP table does not contain an entry for the destination IP address before the first communication attempt.
Expected_Fault: Normal ARP cache miss requires address resolution before data transmission begins.
Expected_Fix: Allow ARP resolution to complete and verify the destination MAC address is learned correctly.
Verification: Repeat communication and confirm the ARP entry is present and response time improves.
Notes: A temporary delay during initial ARP resolution can be normal network behavior.

Symptom: PC1 is connected correctly but cannot communicate with newly added devices until its switchport configuration is updated.
Evidence: show vlan brief shows the required VLAN exists, but the PC interface is assigned to the default VLAN.
Expected_Fault: Access port was not updated after a planned VLAN assignment change.
Expected_Fix: Assign the correct access VLAN to the PC interface.
Verification: Confirm the port appears under the intended VLAN and communication with VLAN members succeeds.
Notes: This is a localized configuration issue with limited network impact.

Symptom: VLAN traffic passes between switches, but an additional VLAN is unavailable across the trunk connection.
Evidence: show interfaces trunk shows the trunk is active but the required VLAN is not included in the allowed VLAN list.
Expected_Fault: Required VLAN is excluded from the permitted trunk VLAN range.
Expected_Fix: Add the required VLAN to the allowed VLAN list on the trunk.
Verification: Verify the VLAN appears as allowed and active on both trunk interfaces.
Notes: The trunk itself works correctly; only one VLAN is affected.

Symptom: Network communication remains functional, but one redundant port is placed in a blocking state.
Evidence: show spanning-tree shows an alternate port not forwarding traffic due to loop prevention.
Expected_Fault: Normal STP operation has blocked a redundant path to prevent a Layer 2 loop.
Expected_Fix: No corrective action is required unless topology design requires a different root bridge.
Verification: Confirm the network remains loop-free and alternate connectivity is available after a link failure.
Notes: A blocked STP port is often expected behavior rather than an actual network fault.

Symptom: After a minor topology change, network connectivity briefly pauses before traffic resumes.
Evidence: Spanning-tree output shows RSTP convergence occurred and port roles changed correctly.
Expected_Fault: Temporary convergence delay occurred during a normal RSTP topology transition.
Expected_Fix: Verify consistent RSTP configuration and monitor for unnecessary repeated topology changes.
Verification: Confirm ports stabilize and communication resumes without manual intervention.
Notes: Short convergence events can occur when redundant network paths change state.

Symptom: EtherChannel is operational, but traffic distribution appears uneven between member links.
Evidence: show etherchannel summary shows all member ports bundled correctly with no suspended interfaces.
Expected_Fault: Uneven traffic is caused by normal load-balancing hash behavior based on traffic flow characteristics.
Expected_Fix: Adjust the load-balancing algorithm only if network requirements demand improved distribution.
Verification: Generate multiple traffic flows and observe utilization across EtherChannel member links.
Notes: A single large flow may use only one physical member link depending on hashing.

Symptom: PC1 communicates successfully, but the displayed hostname or device label causes temporary confusion during troubleshooting.
Evidence: ipconfig confirms a valid IPv4 address, subnet mask, and default gateway despite naming inconsistency.
Expected_Fault: Documentation or host identification mismatch rather than an actual IPv4 connectivity failure.
Expected_Fix: Update device documentation or hostname records to match the assigned network information.
Verification: Verify documentation accurately identifies the device and IP configuration remains functional.
Notes: Proper documentation reduces troubleshooting time and prevents configuration mistakes.

Symptom: PC1 can communicate using IPv6, but multiple IPv6 addresses are displayed and create confusion for the administrator.
Evidence: ipconfig shows both link-local and global unicast IPv6 addresses assigned to the interface.
Expected_Fault: Normal IPv6 addressing behavior is interpreted incorrectly as an address configuration problem.
Expected_Fix: Identify the correct global unicast address for routed communication and document its purpose.
Verification: Confirm communication using the appropriate IPv6 address and gateway.
Notes: IPv6 interfaces commonly have multiple addresses serving different networking purposes.

Symptom: The first ping packet occasionally fails, while subsequent ping packets receive successful replies.
Evidence: Ping statistics show one initial timeout followed by successful replies from the destination.
Expected_Fault: Initial ARP or neighbor discovery resolution delays the first ICMP packet.
Expected_Fix: Repeat the ping test after address resolution has completed.
Verification: Confirm subsequent packets receive replies with stable connectivity.
Notes: The first ping loss may occur while Layer 2 address resolution is taking place.

Symptom: RIP routes are successfully learned, but routing updates generate unnecessary traffic on an unused interface.
Evidence: show ip protocols shows RIP sending updates through an interface with no neighboring RIP router.
Expected_Fault: RIP updates are enabled on an interface where routing advertisements are unnecessary.
Expected_Fix: Configure the unnecessary interface as passive for RIP updates.
Verification: Verify routes remain available while unnecessary update traffic is reduced.
Notes: Passive interfaces improve efficiency without affecting required route advertisement.

Symptom: OSPF adjacency is established and routing works, but hello packets are unnecessarily sent toward a LAN without OSPF neighbors.
Evidence: show ip ospf interface shows OSPF enabled on an interface containing only end devices.
Expected_Fault: OSPF is active on an interface where neighbor formation is not required.
Expected_Fix: Configure the LAN interface as a passive OSPF interface.
Verification: Confirm OSPF routes remain advertised while hello packets are no longer sent unnecessarily.
Notes: Passive interfaces improve security and reduce unnecessary routing protocol traffic.

Symptom: EIGRP routing works normally, but unnecessary hello packets are sent on an interface connected only to end devices.
Evidence: show ip eigrp interfaces displays EIGRP activity on a user-facing LAN interface.
Expected_Fault: EIGRP is unnecessarily active on an interface where no EIGRP neighbor exists.
Expected_Fix: Configure the end-device LAN interface as passive under EIGRP configuration.
Verification: Confirm EIGRP routes continue to be advertised without unnecessary neighbor discovery traffic.
Notes: Passive interfaces are useful for improving routing protocol efficiency and limiting exposure.

Symptom: A TCP application connection is established successfully but closes after a short period of inactivity.
Evidence: Network connectivity is normal and no packet loss is observed during active communication.
Expected_Fault: Application or TCP session timeout closes inactive connections.
Expected_Fix: Adjust the application timeout value if longer inactive sessions are required.
Verification: Keep a test session idle and confirm it remains active for the configured timeout period.
Notes: This is generally a configuration or application behavior issue rather than complete network failure.

Symptom: A UDP application works correctly, but occasional packets are not acknowledged by the receiving application.
Evidence: Packet capture shows UDP datagrams transmitted without acknowledgment or retransmission mechanisms.
Expected_Fault: Normal UDP behavior provides no built-in reliability or acknowledgment.
Expected_Fix: Implement application-level acknowledgment only if reliable delivery is required.
Verification: Monitor application data and confirm expected handling of occasional packet loss.
Notes: UDP prioritizes speed and low overhead over guaranteed delivery.

Symptom: Users can access websites by IP address but experience a brief delay when resolving a new domain name.
Evidence: DNS resolution succeeds after a short delay, and repeated requests respond faster due to cached entries.
Expected_Fault: Initial DNS lookup delay occurs before the hostname information is stored in cache.
Expected_Fix: Verify DNS server responsiveness and allow normal caching to improve repeated lookup performance.
Verification: Repeat the lookup and confirm the hostname resolves successfully with improved response time.
Notes: DNS caching reduces repeated query time and unnecessary traffic to authoritative servers.

Symptom: The website loads correctly, but some static content takes longer to appear than expected.
Evidence: HTTP service is operational and page requests succeed, but large files increase loading time.
Expected_Fault: Large HTTP resources cause increased application response time without complete service failure.
Expected_Fix: Optimize large web resources or enable appropriate caching where required.
Verification: Reload the webpage and confirm reduced loading time for optimized content.
Notes: This is a performance issue rather than a complete HTTP connectivity failure.

Symptom: Users receive a certificate warning while accessing an otherwise functional secure website.
Evidence: HTTPS connection reaches the server, but the certificate name or validity information does not match the accessed hostname.
Expected_Fault: SSL/TLS certificate configuration mismatch causes browser security warnings.
Expected_Fix: Install or configure a valid certificate matching the server hostname and validity period.
Verification: Access the secure website again and confirm the browser accepts the certificate.
Notes: Encryption may still function, but certificate warnings reduce user trust and should be corrected.

Symptom: SSH remote access works, but administrators are required to enter credentials more frequently due to a short session timeout.
Evidence: SSH login succeeds and network connectivity is normal, but inactive sessions close quickly.
Expected_Fault: Configured SSH exec timeout value is too short for the administrator's workflow.
Expected_Fix: Adjust the VTY exec timeout to an appropriate secure value.
Verification: Establish an SSH session and confirm it remains active for the expected period.
Notes: Longer timeouts improve convenience but should be balanced with security requirements.

Symptom: SNMP monitoring works, but the monitoring system receives more information than required from all configured devices.
Evidence: SNMP polling is successful and devices respond, but unnecessary objects are included in monitoring queries.
Expected_Fault: SNMP monitoring scope is broader than operational requirements.
Expected_Fix: Restrict SNMP views or monitoring queries to only required objects and devices.
Verification: Confirm essential monitoring data remains available while unnecessary polling is reduced.
Notes: Proper SNMP scope reduces management traffic and improves monitoring efficiency.
